"I stare into a sterile abyss of patients, our legs lifted. We are industrial products of hope? All with these rare, unique sarcomas... Hard to diagnose. We are here because treatment is an enigma..."

"I wait for my blood. I think of how much that blood must know. It tells me if I must move into the enigma,  I think if there are bad people here getting treatment?   I  could have recommended a restaurant my doctor won't like?  The infusion is beginning  I think too much."

"My doctor calls me in. I tell him that I have been feeling better after the infusions. He says that with drugs like this, patients often say they "feel healthier" when the drugs are working. Fingers crossed, he says. We talk about good Vietnamese and Thai food in the area..."

"Blood results tell the nurses to proceed with the transfusion, a small clear vial, the size of a PEZ dispenser that drips into my arm for an hour. But now I wait. Other patients get different experimental transfusions. They all have a partner. I'm alone..."

"Every two weeks I'm infused with a phase 1 clinical trial immunotherapy drug. Visits vary. Infusion days have been from 7.5 hours to 12 hours days, depends on what the drug trial asks for. Today: Blood has been taken, weight, vitals, EKG. Now I wait for blood results...."

"My girlfriend texts me. I miss her. I'm hungry. I still have over 5 hours here because the infusion hasn't even started. I wish I could have a meeting here, right now. I forgot that my sponsor told me to use the phone and call somebody. I will have time for that later..."

"When I realized I could not live off my old ways any longer, that I would rather die than do the same thing over and over again, I was done. Why does surrender take so long to get to? #RecoveryPosse  #narcoticsanonymous #alcoholicsanonymous"
